narrative.overview: SolarLog is not a dashboard; it is the readout face of a measuring instrument. The surface reads like the panel of a bench meter: a graphite chassis, a single amber needle, and figures etched in monospace so they look measured rather than styled. Depth is denied - panels are separated by hairline 1px seams, never by stacked cards or drop shadows, so the whole screen reads as one continuous instrument face rather than a deck of widgets. The palette is almost monochrome by discipline. Graphite greys carry every chrome, label, and container; the amber accent is spent only on live generation data and the active state, so the one warm hue on the screen always means 'this is the sun, right now.' Green and red are reserved strictly for online/offline truth. The mood is quiet, technical, and trustworthy: the user believes the numbers because they look aferidos, not decorated. The world is mobile-first and column-bound (max 520px). On wide viewports the column does not float in a black void - it seats into a bordered instrument frame with a single structural shadow, the one deliberate exception to the flat rule.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite chassis, hairline 1px seams instead of cards or shadows
Amber reserved for live data and active state only
Monospace tabular figures for every real measurement
Small-caps tracked labels as the panel-header voice
Flat by default; one structural shadow for the desktop frame

rules.name: The Amber-Is-Sunlight Rule
rules.body: Amber (any of its three steps) appears only on live generation data and the active/primary state. If a value is not a live reading and not the one primary action, it is ink, not amber. The accent's scarcity is what makes it legible as 'the sun, now.'

rules.name: The Two-Signal Rule
rules.body: Green means online and red means offline - nothing else. Status color is never used decoratively.

rules.name: The Measured-Figure Rule
rules.body: Every number that is a real reading is set in the monospace tabular face. Sans-serif is for chrome and prose only; a figure in Archivo would read as decoration, not measurement.

rules.name: The Small-Caps Label Rule
rules.body: Section and field labels are always uppercase Archivo with wide tracking (0.1em-0.16em), never sentence-case body text.

rules.name: The No-Shadow-To-Divide Rule
rules.body: Shadows never separate content. Regions divide by 1px Seam lines; shadow is used only to seat the desktop frame, float a toast, or halo the live dot.

dos: Do spend amber only on live generation data and the one active/primary state (The Amber-Is-Sunlight Rule).
Do set every real reading in the monospace tabular face.
Do divide regions with the 1px Seam hairline, not cards or shadows.
Do write section and field labels as uppercase tracked Archivo (small caps).
Do keep inputs at 16px font to prevent mobile zoom.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion - all animation and transition is disabled under it.
donts: Don't use green or red for anything but online/offline status.
Don't add drop shadows to divide or decorate; shadow is only the desktop frame, the toast, and the live-dot halo.
Don't stack content as floating cards; the screen is one continuous instrument face.
Don't set measurement figures in Archivo - that reads as decoration, not instrument output.
Don't let the column free-float on wide screens; seat it in the instrument frame.
